capabilities: Hide selected text as a masked secret via context menu or command palette
Reveal, edit, and save a secret by clicking its mask in Live Preview
Copy the underlying secret value to the clipboard
Restore the original text by removing a secret
Configure the mask symbol and mask length in settings
disambiguation: Not a password manager or secure storage; secrets are stored in the note as reversible base64url encoding, not encryption.
extras: README warns that secrets are base64url-encoded, not encrypted, and that sharing, syncing, or transferring a note may expose them; it explicitly says not to use Veilbit as secure password storage.
problem: Obsidian notes are plain Markdown, so sensitive values like passwords or tokens stay visible to anyone who reads, shares, or syncs the note.

relations.evidence: Copycel copies the secret text instead of the mask when you copy a table cell that contains one.

summary: Masks secret values in notes with a configurable mask and lets you reveal, edit, or copy them on click in Live Preview and Reading view.
